speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I'm Dr. Agent. I understand you've been experiencing fatigue, flank pain, and fever after recently taking antibiotics for sinusitis. To help narrow down the cause, could you describe the exact location of your flank pain and whether it's on one side or both?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling tired, feverish, and I have flank pain. These symptoms continued even after my sinus symptoms improved.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you. To help distinguish between a kidney infection and other causes, are you experiencing any pain or burning when you urinate, or have you noticed any changes in the frequency or appearance of your urine?

speaker: Patient
text: I was first treated with amoxicillin for sinusitis and developed a rash. Then the antibiotic was changed to cephalexin for another week, and the rash went away.

speaker: Doctor
text: That history of a rash followed by fever and flank pain after antibiotics is highly suggestive of acute interstitial nephritis. Have you noticed any decrease in your urine output or any swelling in your legs or around your eyes?

speaker: Patient
text: I do not have nausea, vomiting, or burning with urination. I also have not noticed a major change in urine color.

speaker: Doctor
text: The absence of urinary symptoms makes a typical urinary tract infection less likely, supporting the suspicion of acute interstitial nephritis. To confirm this and assess kidney function, I need to see your lab results. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, Serum Creatinine, Blood Urea Nitrogen

text: The lab results showing leukocyturia with a negative bacterial culture, along with elevated creatinine and urea, strongly confirm acute interstitial nephritis likely triggered by the recent antibiotic use. I have sufficient evidence to make a diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Interstitial Nephritis
